So how can we accomplish meaningful higher education reform? 

First, elect reform-minded governors, which could lead to meaningful campus changes.

The second step: help these governors appoint reform-minded individuals to these boards—easier said than done.

87% of undergraduates in four-year public institutions attend schools where governors control the boards.

Frustration with higher ed is rising—and reformers should focus on the universities governed by pubic boards rather than smaller, elite institutions, @smarick argues in a new @ManhattanInst brief.
